name: write_excel_csv2
title: Write European CSV with a BOM

origin.description: A byte order mark, semicolon separators, and comma decimals.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: The data, path, or collector this function accepts.

origin.details: A byte order mark, semicolon separators, and comma decimals.
origin.value: The same value readr 2.2.0 returns for this case, written as one line in the output.
origin.example:
path <- tempfile()
write_excel_csv2(data.frame(a = 1.5), path)
raw <- readBin(path, "raw", file.info(path)$size)
paste(paste(as.integer(raw[1:3]), collapse = ","), rawToChar(raw[4:length(raw)]), sep = "|")

translation.description: A byte order mark, semicolon separators, and comma decimals.

arguments.name: x
arguments.text: The data, path, or collector this function accepts.

translation.details: A byte order mark, semicolon separators, and comma decimals.
translation.value: The same value readr 2.2.0 returns for this case, written as one line in the output.
translation.example:
path = tempfile.mktemp()
write_excel_csv2(frame(["a"], [[1.5]]), path)
raw = Path(path).read_bytes()
return ",".join(str(value) for value in raw[:3]) + "|" + raw[3:].decode()
